title: Design Google Maps / nearby-places (geospatial, quadtree)
relevance: High — canonical geo HLD (campus + experienced) at Google, Meta, Amazon, Uber, Flipkart/Swiggy-style product cos; probes spatial indexes (geohash / quadtree / S2) + read-heavy LBS. Twin of HQ06 (static POIs vs moving drivers).
company_notes: Campus/new-grad: Yelp/nearby restaurants/Google Maps nearby with geohash + 9 neighbors + Redis cache and light estimation. Experienced (1–4+ YOE): geohash vs quadtree vs S2/H3, hot-cell sharding, cache invalidation, PostGIS vs Redis GEO; full Design Google Maps adds tiles + routing/ETA (Google, Meta, Amazon geo loops; Maps/Flipkart logistics). Highest-signal classic HLD; static twin of ride-hailing proximity with the same geo toolkit.

phases.goal: Lock nearby-places scope (static POIs) vs full Maps extras, plus read-heavy NFRs and scale assumptions.

must_hit.point: Functional core: search places near (lat, lng) within radius R or return top-K nearest; filter by category/type; view place details; admin add/update/soft-delete with eventual visibility.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists nearby search, category filters, place details, and admin writes as the top functional set.

must_hit.point: Default out of scope unless probed: full turn-by-turn navigation, map tile pipeline, reviews/UGC, payments, ads; if interviewer says Design Google Maps, also add location pings, tile serving, A→B routes + ETA.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Scopes aloud to proximity service first, then only expands to tiles/routing when the prompt demands it.

must_hit.point: NFRs: search latency <100–200 ms p99; extremely read-heavy (often cited ~100:1+); global scale but queries are local; slight staleness on place metadata OK.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the p99 latency band, read-heavy ratio, locality of queries, and soft consistency on metadata.

must_hit.point: State assumptions aloud: ~100–200M places globally; discrete radii (500m / 1km / 5km / 20km); return top 20; one region first, then geo-shard.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Verbalizes place count band, discrete radius buckets, top-20 return, and region-then-shard rollout.

probes: What are the top functional requirements for nearby places, and what do you leave out unless I ask for full Google Maps?
What latency and read/write profile are you designing for?

hints.1: Separate the proximity/Yelp-style prompt from the full Maps prompt before listing features.
hints.2: Cover search + filters + details + admin writes, then NFRs: p99 latency, read-heavy ratio, local queries, metadata staleness.
hints.3: Say: nearby within R or top-K, category/open-now filters, place details, eventual admin updates; <100–200 ms p99; ~100:1+ reads; ~100–200M places; radii 500m/1km/5km/20km; top 20; tiles/routing only if full Maps.

phases.goal: Size storage and QPS to justify cache-first reads and a geo index that shrinks candidates before Haversine.

must_hit.point: 200M places × ~500 B metadata ≈ ~100 GB raw (fits sharded SQL/doc; index + replicas larger).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks place × metadata bytes to ~100 GB and notes indexes/replicas grow beyond raw.

must_hit.point: 100M DAU × 10 nearby searches/day ≈ ~10k QPS average; peak 5–10× → design for ~50–100k QPS reads; writes hundreds–low thousands QPS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Derives avg and peak read QPS from DAU × searches/day and contrasts much lower write QPS.

must_hit.point: Hot path working set is popular cells’ place-ID lists + place cards in Redis (GBs–tens of GBs per region), not full photo blobs; Vol 2–style claim that a quadtree for 200M points often fits in memory on a handful of region servers once built.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Puts Redis working set and in-memory regional quadtree in the estimate story, excluding photo blobs from the hot path.

probes: Walk me through storage and QPS for ~200M places and a read-heavy nearby workload.
What does that imply for the read path versus the geo index?

hints.1: Estimate place metadata size and nearby search QPS separately from writes.
hints.2: Use 200M × ~500 B, then 100M DAU × 10 searches/day with a 5–10× peak, and note Redis holds cell lists + cards.
hints.3: ~100 GB raw; ~10k QPS avg → ~50–100k peak reads; writes hundreds–low thousands; Redis GBs–tens of GBs per region; optimize read path + cache so the geo index shrinks candidates before Haversine.

phases.goal: Define nearby search, place detail, and admin write APIs; keep auth on writes and never trust client ranking scores.

must_hit.point: GET /v1/places/nearby with lat, lng, radius_m, category, min_rating, limit, cursor returning places with placeId, name, lat, lng, distance_m, rating, categories[], and optional nextCursor.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches the nearby query params and response fields including distance_m and pagination cursor.

must_hit.point: GET /v1/places/:placeId for details; POST /v1/places and PATCH /v1/places/:placeId for admin create/update with auth on admin writes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows detail read plus authenticated create/patch, and says never trust client-sent ranking scores.

must_hit.point: Optional full-Maps extras: GET /v1/maps/tiles/:z/:x/:y.png (CDN-facing) and POST /v1/directions returning routes with polyline, eta_s, distance_m.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Only adds tile and directions endpoints when the prompt expands beyond nearby places.

probes: Sketch the nearby search and place detail APIs.
What would you add if this were full Google Maps rather than just nearby places?

hints.1: Start with a nearby GET and a place-by-id GET before admin writes.
hints.2: Include radius/category/limit/cursor on nearby; auth only on POST/PATCH; optional tiles and directions for full Maps.
hints.3: Give GET /v1/places/nearby?... → places[] + nextCursor; GET /v1/places/:id; POST/PATCH places; optional /maps/tiles/:z/:x/:y.png and POST /v1/directions → polyline, eta_s, distance_m.

phases.goal: Model Place as source of truth plus a cell→placeIds geo index and Redis result/card caches.

must_hit.point: Place holds placeId, name, address, lat, lng, geohash/s2CellId, categories[], rating, hours, status, updatedAt; PlaceMedia optional and off the search hot path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws Place with a geohash or S2 cell id and keeps media out of the search path.

must_hit.point: Geo index side: cellId → [placeId…] as Redis SET or SQL secondary index; primary DB (Postgres + optional PostGIS, or MySQL + geohash column + B-tree) is source of truth.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates source-of-truth Place storage from the cell-to-placeIds index structure.

must_hit.point: Redis: nearby:{precision}:{geohash}:{category}:{radius} → ranked place IDs (TTL minutes) and place:{id} → JSON card; optionally Redis GEO for live demos; object store + CDN for tiles/photos on the Maps prompt.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows discrete nearby cache keys, place cards, and separates tiles/photos to object store + CDN.

probes: What entities and stores do you need for nearby search?
How do you index places for a radius query?

hints.1: Think Place document plus a spatial cell membership structure.
hints.2: Primary DB for Place; cellId→placeIds index; Redis for nearby results and place cards.
hints.3: Place with geohash/s2CellId; GeoCell lists; Postgres/MySQL source of truth; Redis nearby:{precision}:{geohash}:{category}:{radius} and place:{id}; tiles/photos in object store + CDN if Maps.

phases.goal: Wire API gateway → LBS search with Redis cache, geo index, and Place Service/DB; narrate nearby read and write flows.

must_hit.point: Nearby read: compute cell(s) for (lat,lng,R) → cache lookup → on miss query geo index (9 geohashes or S2 covering or quadtree leaves) → fetch place cards → Haversine filter → rank → cache → return.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Narrates two-phase retrieval: cheap cell/GEO candidates then exact distance filter and rank before caching.

must_hit.point: Write: Place Service upserts DB → update geo membership (old cell → new cell) → invalidate nearby:* keys for affected cells (or short TTL); async cache invalidation / index updater.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Updates DB and cell membership, then invalidates or TTLs nearby cache keys for touched cells.

must_hit.point: Shard by geography (geohash/S2 prefix or city/region) so a NYC nearby query hits 1–2 shards; full Maps adds CDN◄──Tile Store, Navigation (geocoder + route planner + traffic/ETA), and Location Service for high-write pings.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Geo-shards the LBS path and only layers tiles, routing, and location firehose when designing full Maps.

probes: Draw the components for nearby place search and walk a read miss.
What happens on a place update that moves cells?

hints.1: API gateway in front of Place Search, Redis, geo index, and Place Service/DB.
hints.2: Miss path: cells → geo index → cards → Haversine → rank → cache; write path updates membership and invalidates nearby keys.
hints.3: 9 geohashes / S2 covering / quadtree leaves for candidates; never return raw cell contents as within radius; geo-shard so local queries hit 1–2 shards; tiles/routing only for full Maps.

phases.goal: Defend the spatial index choice, Redis/PostGIS read path, and cache-key design for static POIs.

must_hit.point: Geohash: encode (lat,lng) → base32; pick precision from radius (~6 ≈ 0.6 km, ~5 ≈ 2.4 km); query center cell + 8 neighbors; then Haversine (or Redis distance) to refine — never return raw cell contents as within radius.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States precision-from-radius, 9-cell neighbor ring, and exact-distance refine.

must_hit.point: Boundary/edge problem: points meters apart can sit in different cells (or across equator/antimeridian) with short shared prefixes — neighbor ring or S2 coverings is mandatory.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out the classic edge miss without prompting and names the neighbor-ring/S2 covering fix.

must_hit.point: Geohash vs quadtree vs S2/H3: geohash simple/DB-friendly/Redis-native but fixed grid and uneven load; quadtree density-adaptive and good in-memory for static/near-static data but painful under heavy moves; S2 = sphere + Hilbert, region coverings (Google story); H3 = hex k-rings (Uber dispatch/surge).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks one index and accurately contrasts the others on grid vs density vs sphere/hex neighbors.

must_hit.point: Interview default: geohash (or Redis GEO) + Haversine refine + Redis result cache; PostGIS ST_DWithin for correct GIS semantics but still needs replicas/cache at Maps-scale QPS; bucket radius to discrete values in cache keys (continuous free-form radius → ~0 hit rate); for static POIs TTL of 1–5 min is often enough.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defaults to geohash/Redis GEO + cache, names PostGIS as upgrade, and buckets radius with short TTL for static POIs.

probes: Why can’t you just ORDER BY haversine(lat,lng) with B-tree indexes?
Geohash vs quadtree vs S2 — which do you ship and why?
How do you design the nearby cache key?

hints.1: B-trees on lat/lng or sorting by Haversine alone still scan huge candidate sets.
hints.2: Explain 1D locality encoding or a 2D spatial tree, then the neighbor-ring + refine step.
hints.3: Ship geohash/Redis GEO + Haversine + Redis cache for simplicity; quadtree if density skew and mostly static in-memory; S2 if Google-shaped; discrete radius in keys; 1–5 min TTL for static POIs.

phases.goal: Scale hot cells, sparse rings, index lag, and geo shard fan-out without amplifying the read path.

must_hit.point: Hot downtown cells: finer precision, split GEO keys/shards by child cells, more LBS replicas on that region — don’t one-size precision globally.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Tunes precision and sharding per hot region instead of a global fixed cell size.

must_hit.point: Sparse areas: expanding-ring search (widen precision / k-ring) until limit met or max radius; cache place cards, paginate, avoid joining photos on the search path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Widens the ring for sparse results and keeps photos off the search join path.

must_hit.point: Write → index lag: async updater; accept brief stale nearby lists; push invalidation for closures; shard routing via first 2–3 geohash/S2 parent chars with cross-boundary queries fanning out to ≤2 shards.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Accepts short index lag with invalidation for closures and bounds cross-boundary fan-out to ≤2 shards.

probes: How do you handle a very hot downtown geohash cell?
What if a rural query returns too few results inside the first cell ring?

hints.1: Hot spots and empty rural cells need different precision/ring strategies.
hints.2: Split hot child cells and add regional replicas; expand k-ring until limit or max radius.
hints.3: Finer precision + child-cell shards for downtown; expanding-ring for sparse; async index with invalidation on closures; first 2–3 prefix chars → region, ≤2 shards on boundaries; CDN separate from LBS autoscaling.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Geohash is simplest and DB/Redis-native with prefix scans but needs a boundary neighbor ring and has uneven fixed-grid load. Quadtree adapts to density and fits in-memory static/near-static regional indexes, but updates/rebalance are harder and string-key sharding is awkward. S2 indexes on a sphere with Hilbert locality and region coverings—Google’s geography answer—but has more API surface than geohash; H3’s hex k-rings are the contrast when asked why not Uber’s index.

tradeoffs.topic: Redis GEO / cell cache vs PostGIS alone
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Redis GEO or cell cache wins sub-ms candidate fetch for high-QPS nearby reads. PostGIS ST_DWithin gives correct GIS semantics and complex filters but still needs read replicas and a cache at Maps-scale QPS. Interview default is geohash or Redis GEO + Haversine refine + Redis result cache, with PostGIS/S2 named as upgrades.

Bucket radius to discrete values and key by precision + cell + category so hit rate stays high. Invalidate on write via pub/sub/Kafka, or rely on short TTL; for static POIs a TTL of 1–5 min is often enough. Continuous free-form radius params destroy cache usefulness.

tradeoffs.topic: Full Maps preprocessing vs query latency
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Tile pyramid plus contraction hierarchies / preprocessed routing buy ms-level queries at the cost of offline builds; traffic should be overlay multipliers, not a full graph rebuild every minute. Crow-flies Haversine is not drive-time ETA.

tradeoffs.topic: Static POIs vs ride-hailing dynamic geo
tradeoffs.strong_answer: POIs update rarely → DB + Redis result cache keyed by geohash:category:radius. Drivers/users move every few seconds → in-memory GEO/cell sets, short TTL, no multi-minute nearby cache; assignment consistency is hq06, not this problem.

gotchas.trap: SELECT * WHERE distance < R or ORDER BY haversine(lat,lng) as the whole plan
gotchas.correction: You cannot efficiently index that expression alone; filter candidates with a 2D spatial index or locality-preserving encoding first, then refine with Haversine.

gotchas.trap: User on a cell edge misses a restaurant 10 m away
gotchas.correction: Always query the center cell plus the 8 neighbors (9-cell ring) or an S2 covering; boundary/edge misses are the classic trap.

gotchas.trap: Treating this as the same design as Uber nearby drivers
gotchas.correction: POIs are static/read-heavy and cacheable; drivers are write-heavy with consistency on assignment—same geo toolkit, different write/cache story (hq06).
Haversine is only for candidate sort/refine; navigation uses a road graph (A*/contraction hierarchies) plus traffic overlay.

gotchas.trap: Map tiles as one giant Earth image
gotchas.correction: Serve a zoom pyramid of z/x/y tiles from object store + CDN; pan/zoom loads precomputed neighbor tiles.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting to remove deleted/moved places from old cells
gotchas.correction: On write, move geo membership from old cell to new cell and invalidate affected nearby keys, or ghosts appear in nearby results.

gotchas.trap: Caching with unbounded continuous radius query params
gotchas.correction: Bucket radius to discrete values in the cache key; continuous free-form radius yields ~0 hit rate.
